groups.title: Dialog
groups.scope: 29 shared cases; occurrence/page/frame/session ownership, null-page prepublication, UTF-16 metadata, handling, duplicate/stale behavior, page/context listeners/predicates and packed module modes.
groups.limitations: Experimental Chromium/macOS development scope; no native Linux/release/performance acceptance. Page.close({runBeforeUnload:true}) stays unsupported; beforeunload navigation and parent-session cross-process dialog cases do not establish general cross-process frame APIs. Dialog waiter trace capture intentionally omits pinned snapshot references; metadata is bounded to 1 MiB per opening.
groups.defaults: Only the stated subset is reviewed; other defaults remain unverified.

groups.title: ConsoleMessage
groups.scope: Live page/context console delivery and same-process main-world child frames; exact diagnostics, aliases, timestamp, page, null worker, retained original-context argument handles and listener identity/order.
groups.limitations: Worker logs, out-of-process frame delivery and console history remain outside this slice. worker() returns null within verified page scope. BigInt handles and value-derived text preserve values differing from pinned Playwright 1.60.0 (S4.l). 4096 retained/pending handles per page and bounded 4096-ID background release queue.
groups.defaults: Only the stated subset is reviewed; other defaults remain unverified.
differences: Primitive BigInt console arguments and derived text retain their value; pinned 1.60.0 loses that handle value (S4.l).

groups.title: JSHandle
groups.scope: Supported graph values/identity/cycles, nested handle arguments, UTF-16 properties, property ownership, original-context evaluation, DOM detachment, disposal/async disposal, allocation rollback and packed declarations.
groups.limitations: Additional by-value classes remain unsupported; Map/functions/symbols can be retained/evaluated as handles but cannot generally serialize by value. Objects remain in original unique execution contexts; cross-context element adoption and out-of-process frames remain outside this slice. 4096 retained/pending handles per page, bounded replies/serialization and recovery. Primitive BigInt behavior intentionally differs from pinned 1.60.0 (S4.l).
groups.defaults: Only the stated subset is reviewed; other defaults remain unverified.
differences: Primitive BigInt handles preserve the actual JavaScript value; pinned 1.60.0 converts it to undefined (S4.l).

groups.title: ElementHandle
groups.scope: Captured original-node selectText/scrollIntoViewIfNeeded and original-node local-file/buffer/clear assignment. Core report accepted via checkpoint hash includes successful run-element-action-tests and run-file-input-tests.
groups.limitations: JSHandle base operations are inherited; inventory has no duplicated ElementHandle entry for those methods. All other own ElementHandle methods explicitly reject. Same-process frames and same-document temporary utility aliases only; borrowed handle ownership is preserved. Uploads exclude directories/webkitdirectory; 4096 files, 1 MiB metadata, 32768 UTF-16 path units, 32 MiB aggregate memory payloads. Invalid non-file input rejects explicitly, differing from pinned buffer/clear behavior (S4.m).
groups.defaults: Only the stated subset is reviewed; other defaults remain unverified.
differences: File assignment to an INPUT whose type is not file rejects before mutation; pinned buffer/clear behavior silently succeeds and path input retries (S4.m).

groups.title: Tracing
groups.scope: Public manual start/chunk/stop archives, snapshots/screenshots/sources/phase names, exact ownership and actual pinned offline viewer plus packed combined consumers; latest runner follow-up verifies automatic browser-context tracing and public retention policies.
groups.limitations: Live traces, video, group/groupEnd and HAR methods are not implemented in the public Tracing class. live start option rejects through option validation. DOM snapshots cover supported states and same-process frames; unsupported custom-element/out-of-process states fail export explicitly. Public request.newContext remains explicitly unsupported; private native API checkpoints do not establish standalone API request tracing. Manual screenshots/snapshots/sources default false. Runner defaults are separately verified and must not overwrite these manual defaults. Latest public runner checkpoint reuses accepted pre-API trace driver and is focused; no fresh combined full-core/native API/Linux/release/performance acceptance.
groups.defaults: Manual screenshots, snapshots and sources default to false. Omitting a stop path discards the archive. Runner policy defaults are separate.

Browser network routes only; private API request engine does not promote this surface.

groups.title: FileChooser
groups.scope: Chooser page/element/multiplicity identity, original utility-world element despite replacement/detachment, file assignment and same-process child-frame event. Core checkpoint hash proves successful run-file-chooser-tests and run-file-input-tests.
groups.limitations: Removing last listener cancels unpublished native adoption permanently, differing from pinned resubscription race (S4.n). 16 active/queued events per page and 128 per engine; one existing public handle slot per event, bounded background release. Directory/webkitdirectory uploads unsupported; same file limits and invalid-target difference as ElementHandle.setInputFiles. setFiles delegates to original ElementHandle; own options not inferred from shared locator tests without direct fixture assertion.
groups.defaults: Only the stated subset is reviewed; other defaults remain unverified.
differences: Removing the last listener permanently cancels unpublished adoption; a new listener does not receive that cancelled occurrence (S4.n).
File assignment rejects non-file INPUT targets before mutation (S4.m).

groups.title: Keyboard

Page keyboard type retains unbounded public timeout and existing focus; locator deadline/navigation rules do not apply. Linux keyboard checkpoint is amd64 emulation; later full-core checkpoint is macOS development.

groups.title: Automatic runner tracing
groups.scope: Browser-context traces for all eight pinned policy spellings, retention across retries, public stock/module/worker contexts, attachments, source locations and actual pinned viewer loading. 514 public attempts, 21 boundary cases and six viewer cases are retained.
groups.limitations: Live traces, video and public standalone API request tracing remain unavailable. Context creation begun without an attempt owner and published during an attempt reports a trace error. Capture limits and diagnostic failures preserve the original test outcome. Focused macOS acceptance on Bun and Node 22/24; no combined native API, Linux or release acceptance.
groups.defaults: Trace defaults to off. Enabled runner policies use pinned screenshots/snapshots/sources/attachments defaults; boolean overrides are covered. Missing object mode follows the pinned off default.

groups.title: Locator actions and file assignment
groups.scope: Trusted pointer and keyboard actions, fill/selection/focus, checkbox operations, sequential typing, original-node selection/scrolling and listed file-assignment paths have shared native fixture evidence.
groups.limitations: Native frame stability, interception, cancellation and navigation barriers apply. Directory uploads, persistent held keyboard input and unsupported value/target classes remain excluded. Each method claim covers the fixture subset, not all declared action options.

differences: File assignment rejects a non-file INPUT before mutation; pinned buffer/clear and path behavior differ (S4.m).

groups.title: Page and Frame selector actions
groups.scope: Eleven Page/Frame action methods share the native Locator path. The retained 137-check differential covers duplicate matches, strictness, first-match readiness/replacement, native input, selection results, typing focus changes/cancellation, navigation, child-frame ownership, closure and traced calls. Packed library consumers exercise selector forms and declarations.
groups.limitations: Native macOS arm64 development coverage with Bun1.4.2 and Chromium148; controlled capture checks also run on Node22/24. Context strictSelectors, pointer steps, hover noWaitAfter, selectOption ElementHandle values, FrameLocator and broader cross-process frame coverage remain outside this slice. No performance, native Linux or release acceptance.
groups.defaults: Page/Frame selectors use the first match when strict is omitted or false; explicit true rejects multiple matches. Locator remains strict. Ordinary inherited action timeouts and existing method-specific input/navigation behavior remain in force.

groups.title: Lazy same-process FrameLocator paths
groups.scope: Page/Frame/Locator frameLocator, Locator.contentFrame and all FrameLocator descriptor methods. The retained 212-check differential exercises strictness, absence, nesting, same-frame composite normalization, native input/upload, child main-world evaluation, captured targets, whole-path retries, closure and traced forms. Packed consumers exercise runtime exports and declarations.
groups.limitations: Same-process frames on native macOS arm64 with Bun1.4.2 and Chromium148. Out-of-process routing, exhaustive getBy option/value combinations, native Linux, full runtime/consumer matrices, performance and release acceptance remain open. Method coverage is an experimental subset; only separately listed options are promoted.
groups.defaults: Descriptors are lazy and retain their original root Frame. Actions/assertions resolve iframe components strictly; count/list reads use the pinned first iframe match. Page/Frame selector calls retain per-call strictness. Missing iframe behavior is method-specific. Each eligible retry re-resolves the whole path; captured callbacks and uncertain input are never replayed.
differences: Frame-path assertions use ordinary host retry intervals to observe changing ancestor selectors; known-frame assertions retain resident observation.

groups.title: Evaluation and handle resolution
groups.scope: Page/Frame evaluation and Locator evaluation/handle creation preserve supported graph values, original execution context, argument identity and callback lifecycle.
groups.limitations: Supported primitives, arrays/plain objects, dates and regular expressions do not establish arbitrary by-value classes. Same-process frames only. Locator evaluation timeout governs element resolution, not subsequent application callback execution.
groups.defaults: Only the stated subset is reviewed; other defaults remain unverified.
differences: Returned primitive BigInt handles retain their value instead of pinned 1.60.0 handle-path data loss (S4.l).

groups.title: Cookies and storage state
